facts.statement: The genus Anchiceratops was first described by Barnum Brown in 1914.
facts.quote: authority: Brown, 1914

facts.statement: Anchiceratops lived between 73 and 68 million years ago in what is now Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: lived approximately 73 to 68 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: Anchiceratops was a medium-sized, quadrupedal herbivore that could reach a length of 4.3 meters.
facts.quote: Anchiceratops was a medium-sized, heavily built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore that could grow up to an estimated 4.3 m long

facts.statement: Anchiceratops had an elongated, rectangular skull frill with coarse triangular projections along its edges.
facts.quote: The skull frill was elongated and rectangular, its edges adorned by coarse triangular projections

facts.statement: The first Anchiceratops remains were found in 1912 along the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada, by an expedition led by Barnum Brown.
facts.quote: The first remains of Anchiceratops were discovered along the Red Deer River in the Canadian province of Alberta in 1912 by an expedition led by Barnum Brown

facts.statement: Most Anchiceratops fossils come from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.
facts.quote: Most Anchiceratops fossils have been discovered in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta

facts.statement: Remains from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation date to between 72.5 and 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Anchiceratops remains are known from the lower part of the formation, and range in age between 72.5 and 71 million years ago

facts.statement: Frill fragments resembling Anchiceratops have been found in the Almond Formation of Wyoming.
facts.quote: Frill fragments found in the early Maastrichtian Almond Formation of Wyoming in the United States resemble Anchiceratops

facts.statement: Horn and frill fragments dating to 76.5–75 million years ago have been found in the Oldman and Dinosaur Park Formations.
facts.quote: brown horn fragments (specimens NMC 9590 and 10645) and frill pieces (specimens NMC 9813, 9814 and 9829) have been found from two localities in the older Oldman and Dinosaur Park Formations (late Campanian, 76.5-75 million years ago)

facts.statement: Anchiceratops was a quadrupedal herbivore with three facial horns, a parrot-like beak, and a long frill.
facts.quote: Like other ceratopsids, A. ornatus was a quadrupedal herbivore with three horns on its face, a parrot-like beak, and a long frill extending from the back of its head

facts.statement: In Anchiceratops, the brow horns were longer than the nasal horn, a trait shared with other chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: The two horns above the eyes were longer than the single horn on its snout, as in other chasmosaurines

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Anchiceratops weighed 1.2 tonnes and measured 4.3 meters in length based on specimen NMC 8547.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul, on the assumption that specimen NMC 8547 represented Anchiceratops, estimated its length at 4.3 metres, its weight at 1.2 tonnes

facts.statement: The frill of Anchiceratops is edged by large epoccipitals, which are triangular bony osteoderms.
facts.quote: The frill is edged by large epoccipitals, which are osteoderms in the form of triangular bony projections

facts.statement: Anchiceratops possesses a pair of bony knobs on either side of the midline near the rear of the frill.
facts.quote: Another characteristic feature is the pair of bony knobs located on either side of the midline, towards the end of the frill

facts.statement: The frill of Anchiceratops features deep arterial grooves on both its upper and underside surfaces.
facts.quote: The frill has deep arterial grooves on both the upper and the underside

facts.statement: The neck of specimen NMC 8547 is exceptionally long, featuring four fused anterior cervical vertebrae known as syncervicals.
facts.quote: The neck of NMC 8547 is exceptionally long, with four syncervicals, fused anterior cervical vertebrae

facts.statement: Researchers have concluded that differences in skull proportions among Anchiceratops fossils represent different growth stages (ontogeny).
facts.quote: which had led researchers to conclude that the disparity is ontogenetic

facts.statement: It is debated whether horn and frill fragments from the Oldman and Dinosaur Park Formations represent early A. ornatus or a second related species.
facts.quote: These may represent early records of A. ornatus or possibly a second, related species

facts.statement: Barnum Brown assigned the genus Anchiceratops to the Ceratopsia in 1914.
facts.quote: Brown in 1914 assigned Anchiceratops to the Ceratopsia.

facts.statement: William Diller Matthew refined the classification of Anchiceratops to the family Ceratopsidae in 1915.
facts.quote: In 1915, William Diller Matthew refined this to the Ceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Peter Dodson and Phil Currie placed Anchiceratops in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae in 1990.
facts.quote: In 1990, Peter Dodson and Phil Currie placed it in the Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2010 phylogenetic analysis by Ryan et al. confirmed the assignment of Anchiceratops to the Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis conducted by Ryan et al. (2010) confirmed this assignment.

facts.statement: C.M. Sternberg originally designated a smaller skull with slender, forward-pointing horns as the type specimen for the species Anchiceratops longirostris.
facts.quote: C.M. Sternberg had originally designated a smaller skull as the type specimen for a new species Anchiceratops longirostris, because of its size and its horns which are significantly more slender and point forward instead of upward.

facts.statement: The genus Anchiceratops was named by Brown in 1914.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1914

facts.statement: The species A. ornatus was named by Brown in 1914.
facts.quote: species_authority: Brown, 1914

facts.statement: Anchiceratops longirostris is a synonym of Anchiceratops ornatus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Anchiceratops longirostris Sternberg, 1929

facts.statement: Anchiceratops lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 72 to 71 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 y 71 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Anchiceratops specimens are found in the Horsethief member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, dated to about 72 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Anchiceratops specimens are found in the upper part of Unit one of this formation, part of the Horsetheif member, dated to about 72-71 million years ago.

facts.statement: Anchiceratops is rare compared to other ceratopsians and is usually found near marine sediments in the Horseshoe Canyon and Dinosaur Park Formations.
facts.quote: Anchiceratops is rare compared to other ceratopsians in the area, and usually found near marine sediments, in both the Horseshoe Canyon and Dinosaur Park Formations.

facts.statement: Flowering plants were rare compared to conifers, cycads, and ferns, which likely made up the majority of ceratopsian diets.
facts.quote: Flowering plants were increasingly common but still rare compared to the conifers, cycads and ferns which probably made up the majority of ceratopsian diets.

facts.statement: In 1959, Wann Langston Jr. suggested that Anchiceratops had a semi-aquatic lifestyle, using its long snout to cross swamps and its heavy frill as a counterbalance.
facts.quote: In 1959, Wann Langston Jr. suggested that Anchiceratops engaged in a semi-aquatic lifestyle. The long snout would have allowed the animal to cross deeper swamps walking, catching breath on the water's surface and the heavy frill would have acted as a counterbalance to help point the beak upwards.

facts.statement: While later paleontologists rejected the semi-aquatic hypothesis, Mallon suggested in 2012 that at least specimen NMC 8547 lived a semi-aquatic lifestyle similar to a modern hippopotamus.
facts.quote: Later paleontologists tended to reject this notion, emphasizing that dinosaurs in general were land animals, but in 2012 Mallon again suggested a semi-aquatic lifestyle, like a modern hippopotamus, at least for specimen NMC 8547.

facts.statement: In 1990, Thomas Lehman proposed that Anchiceratops was sexually dimorphic, with A. longirostris representing females and larger, more robust skulls with vertical horns representing males.
facts.quote: In 1990 Thomas Lehman proposed that Anchiceratops was a sexually dimorphic genus, where the skull of A. longirostris represents a female. The other Anchiceratops skulls that are larger, more robust, and have much longer horns that point more vertically were proposed to represent males.

facts.statement: Mallon (2012) rejected the hypothesis of sexual dimorphism or two species after statistical analysis showed skull variations represented individual variation rather than distinct morphs.
facts.quote: Preliminary statistical analysis of the Anchiceratops specimens by Mallon (2012) revealed that these variations in skull form do not actually fall into two distinct morphs, and more likely represent individual variation, forcing him to reject the hypothesis that there were two species.

facts.statement: In 2012, Mallon noted that the species Anchiceratops ornatus was exceptionally long-lived compared to other ceratopsid species.
facts.quote: In 2012, Jordan Cole Mallon e.a. pointed out that Anchicertops ornatus as a species was exceptionally long-lived; other ceratopsid species typically last a few hundred thousand years.

facts.statement: Possible explanations for the long lifespan of Anchiceratops ornatus include decreased competition, less habitat fragmentation due to seaway recession, and a generalist lifestyle.
facts.quote: Several possible explanations were given: a decreased competition by related species; less habitat fragmentation by the recession of the Western Interior Seaway; and a more generalist lifestyle.

facts.statement: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation has been radiometrically dated between 74 and 67 million years old.
facts.quote: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation has been radiometrically dated as being between 74 and 67 million years old.

facts.statement: Anchiceratops shared its environment with maniraptorans, ornithomimids, pachycephalosaurids, hadrosaurids, ceratopsians, and tyrannosaurids like Albertosaurus sarcophagus.
facts.quote: Anchiceratops shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, such as maniraptorans (Epichirostenotes curriei), ornithomimids (Ornithomimus edmontonicus), pachycephalosaurids (Sphaerotholus edmontonensis), hadrosaurids (Edmontosaurus regalis), ceratopsians (Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis), and tyrannosaurids (Albertosaurus sarcophagus), which were apex predators.

facts.statement: Hadrosaurs dominated the region in terms of sheer numbers, making up half of all dinosaurs present.
facts.quote: Of these, the hadrosaurs dominated in terms of sheer number and made up half of all dinosaurs who lived in this region.

facts.statement: Anchiceratops was characterized by a long, highly ornamented frill.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por una larga gola, muy adornada.

facts.statement: Anchiceratops ornatus was a quadrupedal herbivore with three facial horns, a parrot-like beak, and a long frill extending from the back of its head.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros ceratópsidos, A. ornatus era un cuadrúpedo herbívoro con tres cuernos en la cara, un pico de loro, y un volante largo que se extiende desde la parte de atrás de su cabeza.

facts.statement: Popular literature estimates Anchiceratops was a medium-sized dinosaur measuring approximately 6 meters in length, 2.6 meters in height, and weighing 1.8 tonnes.
facts.quote: Era un dinosaurio de tamaño mediano, en libros de divulgación se calcula que medía aproximadamente 6 metros de longitud y 2,6 de altura, con un peso estimado de 1,8 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the specimen NMC 8547 of Anchiceratops to be 4.3 meters long and weigh 1.2 tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2010 Gregory S. Paul, calculó para el espécimen NMC 8547 que representa Anchiceratops, 4,3 metros, de largo y un peso de 1,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Anchiceratops possessed three facial horns, bony projections on the sides of its jaw, and a row of spines on its frill, a bony plate resembling the head frills of some dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Poseía tres cuernos en su rostro, protuberancias óseas a los lados de la mandíbula y una fila llena de espinas en su gola (placa ósea de aspecto similar a un volante situado en la parte trasera de la cabeza de algunos dinosaurios).

facts.statement: It had a huge parrot-like beak used to cut stems and tough plants, which were then chewed and crushed by its teeth aligned on the sides.
facts.quote: También presentaba un enorme pico de loro, con el cual cortaba los tallos y plantas duras, las cuales eran luego masticadas y trituradas por sus dientes alineadas a los lados.

facts.statement: The two horns situated above its eyes were longer than the horn located on its snout.
facts.quote: Los dos cuernos situados encima de sus ojos eran más largos que el cuerno emplazado en su hocico.

facts.statement: The frill of Anchiceratops is peculiar, having a rectangular shape with triangular bony projections called epoccipitals along its edges.
facts.quote: La gola de Anchiceratops es muy peculiar. Posee una forma rectangular, presentando, en los bordes, unas protuberancias óseas triangulares llamadas epoccipitales.

facts.statement: The parietal bone forming the rear edge and center of the frill has smaller fenestrae, or skull openings, than those seen in other ceratopsids such as Pentaceratops or Torosaurus.
facts.quote: El hueso parietal , que forma el borde trasero y el centro del volante, tiene menores fenestras, aberturas del cráneo, más pequeñas que las vistas en otros ceratópsidos, tales como Pentaceratops o Torosaurus.

facts.statement: The neck of specimen NMC 8547 is exceptionally long, featuring four synchervicals, or fused anterior cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: El cuello del NMC 8547 es excepcionalmente largo, con cuatro sincervicales, vértebras fusionadas cervical anterior.

facts.statement: Its forelimbs were very robust, featuring a large deltopectoral crest on the humerus, indicating heavy musculature.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores son muy robustas, con una gran cresta deltopectoral en el húmero, lo que indica una musculatura pesada.

facts.statement: American paleontologist Barnum Brown named Anchiceratops in 1914, considering it a transitional form closely related to Monoclonius and Triceratops, intermediate between the two.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo estadounidense Barnum Brown nombró a Anchiceratops en 1914, considerándolo como una forma transicional cercano a Monoclonius y a Triceratops siendo intermedio entre ambos.

facts.statement: The name is derived from the Greek words Agkhi meaning "closely related", Keras meaning "horn", and Ops meaning "face".
facts.quote: El nombre es derivado de las palabras griegas: Agkhi "anchi -/αγχι-" ("cercanamente relacionado"), Keras "cerat-/κερατ-" ("cuerno") y Ops "-ops/ωψ" ("cara").

facts.statement: The first remains of Anchiceratops were discovered along the Red Deer River in the Canadian province of Alberta in 1912 by an expedition led by Barnum Brown.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Anchiceratops fueron descubiertos a lo largo del Río Red Deer en la provincia canadiense de Alberta en 1912 por una expedición liderada por Barnum Brown.

facts.statement: The holotype, AMNH 5251, consists of the rear part of a skull including the long frill and many skull parts found at the same time, with paratypes AMNH 5259 and AMNH 5273 deposited in the American Museum of Natural History in New York City.
facts.quote: El holotipo, AMNH 5251, es la parte posterior de un cráneo, incluyendo el volante largo, y muchas partes de un cráneo encontrado al mismo tiempo, las muestras AMNH 5259 y AMNH 5273 los paratipos, que se encuentran depositados en el Museo Americano de Historia Natural de la ciudad de Nueva York.

facts.statement: A complete skull, NMC 8535, was discovered by C.M. Sternberg in 1924 and described as A. longirostris five years later.
facts.quote: Un cráneo completo, NMC 8535, fue descubierto por C.M. Sternberg en 1924, y descrito como A. longirostris cinco años después.

facts.statement: Another specimen, NMC 8547 or CMN 8547, collected by Sternberg in 1925, lacks the skull but preserves the most complete skeleton for a ceratopsid, including a nearly complete vertebral column missing only the last tail vertebra.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen, NMC 8547 o CMN 8547, recogido por Sternberg en 1925, le falta el cráneo pero preserva el más completo esqueleto para un ceratópsido, entre ello una columna vertebral completa faltándole la última vértebra de la cola.

facts.statement: Most Anchiceratops material was found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, from the early Maastrichtian of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72.5 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: La mayoría del material de Anchiceratops fue descubierto en la Formación Cañón Horseshoe de Alberta, del Maastrichtiense temprano en el Cretácico superior hace aproximadamente entre 72.5 y 71 millones de años.

facts.statement: Frill pieces have also been found in the older Oldman Formation and Dinosaur Park Formation of the late Campanian, 76.5 to 75 million years ago, with the frill nodules seen in Anchiceratops.
facts.quote: Piezas del volante también se han encontrado en las más antiguas Formación Oldman y en la Formación Dinosaur Park, del Campaniaense tardío hace entre 76.5 y 75 millones de años, con las características de los nódulos de la gola que se ven en Anchiceratops.

facts.statement: It has been proposed that Anchiceratops is a sexually dimorphic species, where the A. longirostris skull actually represents a female.
facts.quote: Se ha propuesto que el Anchiceratops es una especie con dimorfismo sexual, donde el cráneo del A. longirostris en realidad representa a una hembra.

facts.statement: This form is thought to correspond to the male, although more information is needed on the topic.
facts.quote: Esta forma se piensa que corresponde a la del macho, aunque se necesite más información del tema.

facts.statement: Skulls differ in proportions, such as supraorbital horn core size or frill dimensions, leading researchers to conclude the disparity results from interspecific differences or sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Los cráneos son diferentes con respecto a sus proporciones, por ejemplo, tamaño de los núcleos de los cuernos supraorbitales o las dimensiones del volante, lo que ha llevado a los investigadores a concluir que la disparidad es el resultado de diferencias interespecíficas o debido a dimorfismo sexual.

facts.statement: A second species named A. longirostris by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1929 is currently considered a junior synonym of A. ornatus.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie llamada A. longirostris por Charles Mortram Sternberg en 1929, pero esta es actualmente considerada sinónimo más moderno de A. ornatus.

facts.statement: The last epiesquamosal is very large, approaching the height of the three osteoderms on each side along the posterior edge of the frill, the epiparietals.
facts.quote: La última epiesquamosal es muy grande, acercándose a la altura de los tres osteodermos por lado en el borde posterior del volante, los epiparietales.

facts.statement: Another characteristic feature is the pair of bony projections located on each side of the midline towards the end of the frill, pointing sideways and varying greatly in shape and size between individuals.
facts.quote: Otro rasgo característico es el par de protuberancias óseas situadas a cada lado de la línea media, hacia el final del volante. Estos están apuntando hacia los lados y son muy variables en forma y tamaño entre los individuos.

facts.statement: Brown assigned Anchiceratops to Ceratopsia in 1914.
facts.quote: Brown en 1914 asignó a Anchiceratops a la Ceratopsia.

facts.statement: William Diller Matthew placed Anchiceratops in Ceratopsidae in 1915.
facts.quote: En 1915, William Diller Matthew lo colocó en Ceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe established the subfamily Chasmosaurinae in the same study where he originally placed Anchiceratops, a classification it retains today.
facts.quote: Irónicamente, en el mismo estudio Lambe erigido Chasmosaurinae, el taxón al que Anchiceratops se asigna a la actualidad.

facts.statement: Peter Dodson and Phil Currie placed Anchiceratops in Chasmosaurinae in 1990.
facts.quote: En 1990, Peter Dodson y Phil Currie lo colocaron en el Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Ryan et al. in 2010 confirmed the placement of Anchiceratops within Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético realizado por Ryan et al. (2010) confirmaron esta asignación.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analyses generally place Anchiceratops in a more advanced position within Chasmosaurinae, closer to Arrhinoceratops than to Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: Modernos análisis cladísticos generalmente recuperan a Anchiceratops en una posición más avanzada dentro de Chasmosaurinae, más cerca de Arrhinoceratops que de Chasmosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Mallon concluded that Anchiceratops is more closely related to Chasmosaurus than to Triceratops, suggesting the genus is less derived than previously thought.
facts.quote: El estudio de 2012 de Mallon concluyó sin embargo, que Anchiceratops estaba más estrechamente relacionado con Chasmosaurus que a Triceratops, lo que sugiere que este género menos derivado de lo que se pensaba.

facts.statement: Sternberg originally designated a smaller skull as a new species, Anchiceratops longirostris, because its horns were significantly thinner and pointed forward instead of upward.
facts.quote: Sternberg había designado originalmente un cráneo más pequeño que el espécimen tipo para una nueva especie Anchiceratops longirostris, debido a su tamaño y sus cuernos, que son significativamente más delgados y apuntan hacia adelante en lugar de hacia arriba.

facts.statement: In 2010, Mallon removed specimen NMC 8547 from the Anchiceratops fossil record due to its few cranial elements and uncertainty regarding its taxonomic affiliation.
facts.quote: En 2010 Mallon retira al espécimen NMC 8547 del material fósil de Anchiceratops debido a los pocos elementos volante del misma y porque no se pudo determinar con certeza si el material pertenecía a este taxón.

facts.statement: The parent group of Anchiceratops is Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Chasmosaurinae

facts.statement: Anchiceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Anchiceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Anchiceratops is Anchiceratops ornatus.
facts.quote: Type species: Anchiceratops ornatus

facts.statement: Anchiceratops lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
